design.quote: This study is a secondary analysis of data from a randomized controlled trial carried out between October 2020 and October 2023.

population.quote: Adults with obesity in the Minneapolis-Saint Paul, Minnesota, metropolitan area who completed study baseline and follow-up measures of dietary intake (n = 73).
population.value: Adults with obesity in the Minneapolis-Saint Paul, Minnesota, metropolitan area

sample_size.quote: Adults with obesity in the Minneapolis-Saint Paul, Minnesota, metropolitan area who completed study baseline and follow-up measures of dietary intake (n = 73).

intervention.quote: The interventions were (1) TRE with an 8-hour self-chosen window with ad libitum diet;
intervention.value: TRE with an 8-hour self-chosen window with ad libitum diet

comparator.quote: The interventions were (1) TRE with an 8-hour self-chosen window with ad libitum diet; (2) ER diet with 15% reduction of energy intake; or (3) UE in which self-monitoring of food intake was encouraged with no specific change to eating recommended.

primary_findings.quote: The TRE group ate fewer daily meals at end-intervention (-1.1 meals/day; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.6, -0.7) compared with baseline.
Those in the TRE group were less likely to report eating breakfast during end-intervention compared with baseline (odds ratio [OR], 0.13; 95% CI, 0.05, 0.33).
Between baseline and end-intervention those in the TRE group had a decrease in intake of energy (-469 kcal/day; 95% CI, -681, -257).
Between baseline and end-intervention those in the TRE group had a decrease in intake of saturated fat (-8.5 g/day; 95% CI, -12.9, -4.1).
Between baseline and end-intervention those in the TRE group had a decrease in intake of potassium (-496 mg/day; 95% CI, -729, -263).
